record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Describe finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents, where a Lesokhin semigroup is a commutative semigroup whose endomorphisms are all power maps sending each element to a fixed power of itself.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.5. (A.A. Borisov) Describe finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempo-
tents.
It is proved in [5] that finitely generated separative Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents should
be isomorphic to subsemigroups of an infinite monogenic semigroup.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a commutative semigroup. An endomorphism of $S$ is a map $\varphi : S \to S$ satisfying $\varphi(xy) = \varphi(x)\varphi(y)$ for all $x,y \in S$. A power function on $S$ is a map of the form $x \mapsto x^n$ for some fixed positive integer $n$ (the same $n$ for all $x \in S$). Call $S$ a Lesokhin semigroup if every endomorphism of $S$ is a power function. An element $e \in S$ is idempotent if $e^2 = e$.

Give a complete description (classification) of all finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups that contain no idempotent elements.

(It is known that within the separative case, every such semigroup is isomorphic to a subsemigroup of an infinite monogenic semigroup; the problem asks for a description in the general finitely generated case without idempotents.)
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents appears to be only partially resolved. The 2-generated case without idempotents has been characterized (such semigroups are exactly the subsemigroups of an infinite cyclic semigroup), and the separative case is known. A general classification for arbitrary finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents does not appear to be available in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Commutative semigroups whose endomorphisms are power functions
status_evidence.snippet: Every endomorphism of a 2-generated commutative semigroup S without idempotent is a power function if and only if S is a subsemigroup of an infinite cyclic semigroup.
status_evidence.claim: The 2-generated subcase of the problem has been solved.

status_evidence.snippet: Problem 3.5 (A.A. Borisov): Describe finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents.
